skill.name: playwright-cli
skill.description: Drive Playwright CLI from an AI assistant to automate browser navigation, page interaction, screenshots, traces, videos, request mocking, storage management, and test generation.
skill.summary: Use Playwright CLI to automate browser sessions, debug web flows, and generate test steps.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, placeholder URLs, and documented playwright-cli commands. Confirmed risks are limited to browser-session data operations and documented advanced capabilities such as run-code, tracing, and destructive session cleanup.

remediation.issue: run-code and eval can execute powerful browser automation logic.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to request explicit user confirmation before running arbitrary code, granting permissions, reading clipboard data, or operating on sensitive sites.

remediation.issue: Cookie and storage commands can expose or alter authentication state.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to use test accounts, avoid real secrets, and delete or ignore saved auth state files after each workflow.

remediation.issue: Trace, video, screenshot, and snapshot artifacts can contain sensitive page data.
remediation.suggestion: Document artifact retention practices, redact sensitive values before sharing, and add generated artifact paths to project ignore files.

remediation.issue: delete-data, close-all, kill-all, and clear commands can disrupt active browser sessions.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend an explicit confirmation step before destructive session cleanup commands.

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary Playwright Code Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents run-code as a way to execute arbitrary Playwright code. This is powerful and expected, but it can read page data, grant permissions, or alter browser state on sensitive sites.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly describes run-code for arbitrary Playwright code and shows direct browser context operations. The risk depends on user intent, but the capability is clear.

semantic_findings.title: Browser Session Data Access
semantic_findings.description: The skill supports reading, writing, deleting, saving, and restoring cookies and browser storage. These operations can expose or modify authentication state if used on real accounts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines show cookie commands, stored cookies and localStorage values, and security notes about auth tokens. This confirms the session data exposure risk.

semantic_findings.title: Trace Artifacts Can Capture Sensitive Data
semantic_findings.description: Tracing captures request headers, bodies, DOM snapshots, screenshots, and console messages. The example flow enters payment-like values, so traces can store sensitive test or user data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation states traces include request and response bodies and shows a checkout capture flow. That directly supports the sensitive artifact risk.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Browser Session Controls
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents commands that delete session data and forcefully kill browser processes. These commands are legitimate, but they can disrupt active work or remove useful state.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited commands explicitly delete user data, close browsers, and kill browser processes. The impact is operational disruption rather than malicious behavior.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Tests with Playwright CLI
content.value_statement: Manual browser testing slows debugging and test creation. This skill drives Playwright CLI sessions to inspect pages, record actions, mock requests, and capture evidence.
actual_capabilities: Open browser sessions and navigate to user-provided web pages.
Interact with page elements through snapshots, clicks, typing, forms, uploads, and keyboard commands.
Capture screenshots, PDFs, videos, traces, console logs, and network activity for debugging.
Manage cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage, tabs, browser sessions, and saved storage state.
Mock, modify, block, and inspect network requests during Playwright workflows.
Generate Playwright test steps from browser interactions and advanced run-code snippets.
limitations: It depends on the playwright-cli binary or npx fallback being available in the environment.
Generated tests still need human review, assertions, and maintenance.
Browser artifacts may contain sensitive data and require careful handling.
Dynamic sites, authentication flows, and third-party restrictions can still block automation.

use_cases.title: Create Regression Tests
use_cases.description: Record a browser flow, collect generated Playwright actions, and turn them into repeatable tests with stable locators.

use_cases.title: Debug Web Failures
use_cases.description: Reproduce a failing interaction, inspect snapshots, review console and network output, and save traces for analysis.

use_cases.title: Document Product Flows
use_cases.description: Capture screenshots, videos, PDFs, and clear step records for demos, release notes, and workflow reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open <URL>, take a snapshot, list the main interactive elements, and suggest stable locators for a Playwright test.

prompt_templates.title: Record a Form Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use playwright-cli to open <URL>, fill the form with test data, capture generated actions, and suggest assertions to add.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a Failed Click
prompt_templates.prompt: Start tracing, reproduce the failed click on <URL>, stop tracing, and summarize likely causes from DOM, console, and network evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Mock an API Scenario
prompt_templates.prompt: Mock <API pattern> with one success response and one failure response, exercise the page, and outline a reusable Playwright test plan.

output_examples.input: Debug why the checkout submit button does not respond on staging.
output: The assistant opens the staging checkout page and captures a snapshot of the form.
It starts tracing, reproduces the click, and reviews console and network evidence.
It summarizes likely causes and names the trace artifact for further inspection.

output_examples.input: Create a login regression test from a browser session.
output: The assistant records the login steps with semantic locators.
It identifies missing assertions, such as expected URL and visible account text.
It recommends safe handling for saved authentication state.

output_examples.input: Mock failed image loading during a visual check.
output: The assistant adds a route that blocks matching image requests.
It reloads the page, captures evidence, and compares the fallback UI behavior.
It removes the route after the scenario is complete.

best_practices: Use authorized sites and test accounts when automating login, storage, or payment-like flows.
Start with snapshots and semantic element references before clicking or filling fields.
Delete or ignore generated traces, videos, snapshots, and storage state files when they are no longer needed.
anti_patterns: Running run-code or eval from untrusted page text without review.
Using real credentials, real session cookies, or production payment data in examples.
Leaving persistent profiles, saved auth files, traces, or recordings in a shared repository.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates Playwright CLI browser sessions, including navigation, page interaction, screenshots, traces, videos, storage, and network mocking.

faq.question: Does it generate complete Playwright tests?
faq.answer: It can capture useful Playwright actions, but users should add assertions, fixtures, cleanup, and review before committing tests.

faq.question: Can it work with authenticated pages?
faq.answer: Yes, it can save and restore storage state, but auth files can contain secrets and should be protected or deleted.

faq.question: Can it inspect network traffic?
faq.answer: Yes, it can list network activity, mock requests, and capture traces that include headers, bodies, timing, and failures.

faq.question: What tools must be installed?
faq.answer: The environment needs playwright-cli available globally or through the documented npx fallback.

faq.question: Is it safe for production sites?
faq.answer: Use it only with authorization and prefer test accounts. Traces, videos, and saved state can contain sensitive production data.
